# Slides editor: editing on the canvas

The Slides editor (Slides → open a deck) edits elements directly on the slide, the way
PowerPoint does. Everything below applies to decks you build by hand, decks made with
**Make a sign**, and decks generated by AI.

## Selecting

- **Click** an element to select it. A selected element shows resize handles: eight on
  boxes, photos, QR codes and rules; two (left and right) on text, because a text box is
  as tall as its words.
- **Shift-click** or **Ctrl/Cmd-click** adds an element to the selection, or removes it.
- **Drag on an empty part of the slide** to draw a selection box. It picks up every element
  it fully encloses (hold Shift or Ctrl to add to the current selection).
- **Click an empty part of the slide** or press **Esc** to deselect.
- **Ctrl/Cmd+A** selects every element on the slide.
- The layers list under the inspector tabs selects the same way (Shift/Ctrl-click for more
  than one).

## Moving and resizing

- **Drag** an element to move it. With several selected, they move together.
- **Arrow keys** nudge the selection by 1% of the slide; **Shift+arrow** by 10%.
- **Drag a handle** to resize. Photos and lettering keep their shape; hold **Shift** to free
  them (and to keep the shape of anything else). Hold **Alt/Option** to resize from the centre.
- While you drag, edges and centres **snap** to the slide's edges and centre and to the other
  elements, and a pink guide line shows what lined up. Hold **Alt/Option** while moving, or
  switch off the magnet button in the toolbar, to place freely.
- The Style tab's X, Y, Width and Height numbers follow the drag as it happens, and typing a
  number there moves the element.
- On a tablet, drag with a finger. The handles are larger on a touch screen.

## Arrange toolbar and right-click menu

The toolbar above the slide, and the menu you get by right-clicking an element, offer:

| Action | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| Undo / Redo | Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y |
| Bring to front / Send to back | Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+] / Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+[ |
| Bring forward / Send backward | Ctrl/Cmd+] / Ctrl/Cmd+[ |
| Align left, centre, right, top, middle, bottom | (toolbar) |
| Distribute horizontally / vertically (three or more) | (toolbar) |
| Cut / Copy / Paste | Ctrl/Cmd+X / C / V |
| Duplicate | Ctrl/Cmd+D |
| Delete | Delete or Backspace |

With one element selected, the align buttons line it up with the slide; with several, with
each other. A copy or duplicate is a new element with its own identity and the same words, so
editing one never changes the other. Pasting works on another slide of the same deck too.

Keyboard shortcuts work while the slide editor has focus. They stay out of the way while you
type in a field or in the AI prompt, so Ctrl+Z there undoes your typing, not the slide.

## Editing text in place

**Double-click** a headline, text or big-number element to type straight onto the slide.
**Enter** finishes (Shift+Enter starts a new line), **Esc** cancels, and clicking elsewhere
finishes too.

## Undo

Every change to the deck can be undone: moves, resizes, arrange, align, clipboard, deletes,
in-place text and the inspector's controls. Dragging a slider is one step, and so is holding
an arrow key down. The history keeps the last 100 steps and is cleared when you close the deck.
Saving does not clear it.

## Not included

- **Rotation.** The renderer's entrance animations move elements with CSS transforms, so a
  rotated element would turn upright while it animated in, and the separate CSS `rotate`
  property is missing from the Android WebView versions many signage panels still run. It
  needs a change to how every player draws a slide, so it was left out rather than shipped
  half-working.

## For administrators

Nothing to configure. What a screen plays is unchanged. The deck format is unchanged.
When a deck is opened, any two elements on one slide that share a field name ("slot") are
given separate ones, with the words copied, so each shows exactly what it showed before.
This becomes part of the deck the next time it is saved.
